title: The Product Step Ladder
overview: Vishen opened Day 2 by showing you the one-page flow chart behind Mindvalley's $100 million business and the idea that sits underneath it: the product step ladder. You learned why selling a single product caps your growth, how a free experience leads into low-ticket, flagship, group and mastermind offers, and how to make every upsell feel like a helpful guide rather than a pushy salesperson. You also met Nora Cabani, a student who applied these ideas and grew her business 300% in three months and 1,100% in a year.
key_ideas: Your biggest mistake may not be your marketing, content or audience size but that you only sell one thing. Most experts run a restaurant that serves one excellent dish, only on Tuesdays, with no menu for the customer who comes back on Wednesday. Of roughly 8,000 attendees surveyed before the summit, 73% earn under $25,000 a year from their expert business and 23% earn between $25,000 and $500,000; growth is costing you hours, and the ladder is how you grow without adding hours.

Ray Kroc's McDonald's model: would you like fries with that (upsell 1), add a Coke (upsell 2), supersize it (upsell 3). One purchase becomes three. McDonald's could keep the burger cheap because it made its money on the fries and the Coke. Your first product should simply break even and pay for advertising; the profit comes from products two and three.

The Mindvalley funnel in real numbers: a masterclass sells the Silva Ultramind quest at $99 to $149; upsell 1 adds a $79 companion programme; if declined, a $29 downsell of a different product; then continuity via the meditation app at $99 a year, price locked for life. Day one only breaks even. Profit arrives on day 21 (an offer for Lifebook) and day 90 (an invitation to a summit), after three weeks of making sure the customer is having a great experience.

Upsell as a friendly guide, not a used-car salesman. Vishen contrasted the pushy dealer who ripped the clipboard from his hands over a 1989 Honda Accord with the later salesperson who explained how to save $300 and threw in the spare tyre. He bought from both, but only ever recommended the second. Make the next offer a genuine service, and make refunds one click.

Where you ask matters more than what you charge. Tony Robbins does not sell his $10,000 programme by email; it is sold on day 3 of a live event. Mindvalley sells its $5,000 programmes from the summit stage, not by email. Your first ask is always free.

The maths of the ladder: only about 3% of your list will ever buy, and roughly 3% of those buyers produce 48% of your revenue. One buyer at $7,500 brings in more than 100 buyers at $49. This is why you must nurture every customer into a raving fan.

Three levels of building an expert business: Level 1 is understanding smarter systems (takes you to about $1 million), Level 2 is optimisation with AI helping on pages and copy (to $10 million), Level 3 is automation where AI runs parts of the business (to $100 million). Vishen showed Mindvalley's Page Builder AI cutting a two-week page build to 20 minutes and its CRO AI finding, at 95% confidence, a 115% lift from selling a single $99 programme rather than a $199 bundle. Eight Sleep's automated email AI now generates $100 million in revenue. If done right, your team size stays the same across all three levels.

Nora Cabani, founder of Alba Health, sat where you are a year ago with under 1,000 followers and almost no sales. She picked a few things to implement immediately: a free assessment quiz (built in Typeform in three days, taken by over 20,000 people), masterclasses and email marketing. Three months later revenue was up 300% with ad costs cut 50%; a year later she had grown 1,100%, been named a top 10 innovator in Italy and had an open letter to the British government answered and published in The Guardian.

frameworks.name: The Product Step Ladder
steps: Rung 1, Free experience ($0): earn permission to contact them with a webinar, quiz, challenge, checklist or white paper.

Rung 2, Low-ticket offer ($27 to $97): turn a follower into a buyer with a single meditation, a chapter, a short book, a recorded workshop or a template pack. Resist charging $1,000 here even if the content is life-changing.

Rung 3, Flagship programme ($297 to $997; Mindvalley's range is $49 to $399): the course you are most passionate about, typically sold from a 60-minute masterclass with 45 minutes of teaching and 15 minutes of selling.

Rung 4, Group coaching programme ($1,000 to $2,997; Mindvalley's Mastery programmes are $5,000): offered about a month after the flagship purchase to work with students to get results, with strong community.
Rung 5, Mastermind for superfans ($5,000 to $25,000; Mindvalley's is $10,000 a year, application only): peers accelerating each other's businesses, or one-to-one coaching over a year.
The pricing rule: every rung up multiplies the price roughly five times, for example $20, $100, $500, $5,000, $25,000.
The loop: when someone finishes one ladder, loop them into a new one (Mindvalley's AI ladder feeds its entrepreneurship ladder, which feeds its expert-to-authority ladder).

frameworks.name: Three Levels of Building an Expert Business
steps: Level 1, Understanding: smarter systems, principles and models such as webinars, product pipelines, Cialdini's principles and copy. Gets you from $20K to $50K up to $1 million.
Level 2, Optimisation: bring in AI to optimise your pages, help with your copy and help write your webinar. Gets you to $10 million.
Level 3, Automation: the AI runs the business, like a dark factory where robots work without lights. Gets you to $100 million with the same team size.

frameworks.name: The Ladder Question (ask it five times)
steps: What do they buy once that worked?
Repeat until you have five rungs.

exercises: Map your ladder (Vishen's homework for later today). Write down: What do you sell now? What is the rung above it? What is the rung below it? What in your ladder might be in the wrong place? Which type of customer could your ladder be losing on day one (for example, someone not ready to spend $200 on your course who would happily pay $5 for one lesson)?
If you have not sold anything yet, build the middle rung first: one flagship course. Do not try to create all five rungs at once; build them in phases, with your customers.
next_steps: Complete the map-your-ladder questions and sketch all five rungs with a rough price for each, using the five-times rule.
Pick one missing rung you can add fastest, most likely a low-ticket product carved from what you already teach (a single meditation, chapter or template pack).
Rewrite your current upsell or next-offer message as a helpful guide: explain why it helps at that exact moment and make it easy to skip and easy to refund.
Decide where each offer will be asked for (email, masterclass, live event) rather than only what it will cost.
